# aios-kit

`aios-kit` is a lightweight, portable, agent-friendly Personal AIOS installation and distribution kit.

It is not about "installing a few more AI tools." Instead, it establishes an Agent-readable local foundation for your projects, knowledge, services, scripts, skills, and long-running tasks: humans express goals, Agents formulate strategies, CLI/API tools execute deterministic actions, and file-based state preserves facts and evidence.

## Current Status

`aios-kit` is still under rapid development and in maintainer preview. The public one-click installation entry point has been temporarily withdrawn; stable installation, upgrades, and cross-platform compatibility are not currently guaranteed for general users.

The installers and installation documentation in this repository remain available for development and validation. To evaluate the project or contribute to development, first read the [Development Guide](docs/development.md), [Security and Privacy Boundaries](docs/security-and-privacy.md), and [Evolution Roadmap](docs/evolution.md). Begin by reviewing the source and running a dry run in an isolated environment.

### Evaluate and Install Through an Agent (Currently Recommended)

Give the repository URL and the following objective to a trusted terminal Agent, such as Hermes, Codex, or Claude Code. The Agent should read the project files and adapt to the current platform instead of blindly copying fixed commands:

```text
Please evaluate and help install aios-kit: https://github.com/LinLin00000000/aios-kit
First read the README, installation, security, development, and evolution documentation in the repository. Identify the current platform and the boundaries of features still under development.
Review the installation scripts and run a dry run first. Explain which paths and system settings will be modified, the platform limitations, and how to roll back. Perform the actual installation only after receiving my confirmation.
Do not read, print, or commit secret values, subscription URLs, tokens, keys, or private configuration.
```

## Current Capabilities Overview

### Core Modules and Directories

| Module / Capability | Installation Location | Default Platforms | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIOS instance root | `~/aios` | Linux / Windows; macOS supports exploratory dry runs | Keeps the Personal AIOS state, modules, work directories, and cache within a portable boundary | Use `--root` to change the path |
| `aios-kit` module | `~/aios/modules/aios-kit` | Linux / Windows | Source of the installer, `aios` CLI, skillpack manifest, documentation, and templates | Update with `aios update modules` on Linux/WSL |
| LLL module | `~/aios/modules/lins-living-loop` | Linux / Windows | File-based foundation for long-running tasks and Agent workflows | The module is installed on native Windows; Git Bash/WSL/Linux is still recommended for the complete `lll` CLI |
| Command entry points | `~/aios/bin/aios`, `~/aios/bin/lll`; `.ps1/.cmd` shims on Windows | Linux / Windows | Provides stable entry points for Agents and humans without requiring them to remember repository paths | Can optionally be added to PATH |
| Work directory | `~/aios/work` | Designed for all platforms | LLL / Agent work directory for long-running tasks, research, validation, and deliverables | Persistent work layer outside conversations |
| Derived Matter indexes and views | `~/aios/state/matters`, `~/aios/view/matters` | Linux / Windows | Queries active/paused/closed/archived matters across Worksites and provides read-only access to selected deliverables | Rebuildable; does not replace Worksite files as the source of truth |
| Configuration/state/logs/cache | `~/aios/config`, `state`, `logs`, `cache` | Designed for all platforms | Stores instance configuration, installation state, logs, and cache | Prevents data from being scattered across implicit locations |
| Private vault boundary | `~/aios/vault/ops` | Initialized by default on Linux; core directories created on Windows | Stores private facts such as the OPS vault, project registry, and maintenance records | Keeps public templates separate from actual private data |
| Runtime skills target directory | `~/.agents/skills` by default, with an optional Hermes target | Full synchronization on Linux / WSL; native Windows initializes the target first | Location from which the Agent actually loads skills | Does not take over the entire skills directory; managed skills are installed individually |

## Vision and Design Philosophy

The goal of Personal AIOS is simple: turn AI from a "temporary chat assistant" into an operational layer that can work continuously with your real digital world. It needs to know where projects are located, how to inspect services, where the boundaries for data and secrets lie, which work can be automated, and which actions require confirmation.

`aios-kit` provides only the minimal skeleton for this operational layer: unified directories, managed skills, a resource registry, an OPS vault, an LLL workflow entry point, and installation/update/inspection commands. It does not attempt to absorb every tool. Instead, it gives different Agents and tools a shared anchor in reality.

Design trade-offs:

| Principle | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| Agent-first | Commands, documentation, registries, vaults, and logs must be easy for Agents to discover, parse, and recover; human commands are the fallback. |
| Files are the source of truth | Important facts are persisted in the vault / registry / workdir / manifest instead of being trapped in a single conversation. |
| Thin control plane | `aios` handles discovery, installation, updates, and health checks; LLL, Hermes, Mihomo, and other components retain their own state machines. CLI/API tools are Agent actuators, not commands for ordinary users to memorize. |
| Separation of private and public data | The public repository contains only templates, scripts, skills, and structure; actual assets, secrets, subscriptions, maintenance logs, and local overlays remain in the local vault/state. |
| Incremental evolution | Prioritize module breadth and keep each capability focused; new capabilities must demonstrate that they reduce more system complexity than they introduce. See [docs/evolution.md](docs/evolution.md). |
| Self-iteration | When Agents discover failure modes, unnecessarily long paths, or validation gaps while using AIOS, they should proactively propose or record improvements to skills, documentation, CLI tools, validation scripts, and workflows. |
| Portable rather than platform-locked | Default paths are explicit, backup-friendly, and reinstallable; Hermes is the default hub, but not the only Agent. |

## Default Directory Structure

```text
~/aios/
  bin/                     # aios / lll command entry points
  config/                  # Instance configuration
  vault/ops/               # OPS vault boundary: template structure + private facts entry point
  work/                    # LLL / Agent work directory
  skills/                  # AIOS metadata/cache, not the runtime skills directory
  modules/                 # Updatable module checkouts
  network/mihomo/          # Optional Mihomo network component
  state/ logs/ cache/
```

Runtime skills actually loaded by an Agent are still installed in the Agent's own directory, such as `~/.agents/skills/<skill>` or `~/.hermes/skills/<skill>`. The Linux/WSL backend installs managed skills individually and does not take over the entire skills directory. Native Windows installation currently initializes the skills target directory first; managed skillpack synchronization is still recommended through WSL/Linux.

## LLL Workflow Entry Point

LLL (Lin's Living Loop) is one of the workflow foundations of AIOS, but it remains an independent, first-class CLI. `aios-kit` is responsible for discovering, installing, updating, and governing LLL without absorbing its core state machine.

```bash
./aios update modules lins-living-loop
./aios lll doctor --json
./aios lll list --json
./aios lll new demo --objective "..."
./aios lll status <workdir-or-name> --json
```

The boundary of `aios lll ...`: by default, it only locates the `lll` CLI/helper, lists LLL workdirs under the AIOS work root, creates new workdirs, or delegates status/validation to `lll`. Task queues, runners, leases, reapers, and artifacts remain the responsibility of the LLL CLI/protocol. A standard installation exposes both the `aios` and `lll` commands in `~/aios/bin/`; `aios lll doctor --json` checks the LLL version in the AIOS module first to avoid being misled by an outdated version on PATH.

## Networking and Mihomo

The installer first tests external connectivity without setting proxy environment variables. If the direct connection fails, interactive mode asks whether to install Mihomo, defaulting to yes; non-interactive `--proxy auto` installs it automatically.

Mihomo is installed in `~/aios/network/mihomo` by default, with TUN enabled by default. On Linux/systemd, it creates `aios-mihomo.service`. TUN configuration is not universally portable across Windows/macOS/Linux; the current defaults primarily target Ubuntu/Debian cloud servers. For details, see [docs/mihomo-network.md](docs/mihomo-network.md).

## Common Commands

Agents should prefer JSON/doctor/status probes. Humans should execute commands manually only as a fallback for troubleshooting:

```bash
aios status                 # Show an instance summary (human-readable)
aios doctor                 # Validate installation and link state (human-readable)
aios doctor --json          # Compact aios.doctor.v1; ok matches the exit code, with diagnostics centrally redacted
aios update --dry-run       # Preview updates
aios update                 # Update modules, OPS templates, and managed skills
aios update skills          # Refresh managed runtime skills
aios project list           # Show the project/resource registry
aios source list            # Show the explicit Source + Project federated projection
aios source validate        # Validate Source identity / policy / locator structure
aios lll doctor --json      # Agent-first: inspect LLL/Code Loop capabilities
aios lll list --json        # Agent-first: enumerate LLL workdirs
```

Maintenance/debugging entry points: `aios skillpack doctor`, `aios skillpack sync --dry-run`, and `aios assets doctor`. If PATH is not configured, use `~/aios/bin/aios status` or `~/aios/bin/lll --version`.
